Axiom: A reported symptom is an entry point, never the class. Every finding MUST be classified BEFORE any edit: bug vs spec-defect, ownership, semantic vs editorial spec impact, action category (bounded-direct / authoring-flow / task-continue / ticket-create-or-recover), the full problem class, and the blast radius. Code with one resolver-confirmed `active` relation may continue/recover only that ticket under its state policy. With no active relation, route through the resolved `@spec` owner to select, create, or recover maintenance work; `planned`, `blocked`, and `history` are evidence for that spec-level selection, never direct routing authority. A semantic spec change ALWAYS routes through the artifact-kind authoring flow, independent semantic review, and operator approval #1 lifecycle before implementation. Direct editing is reserved for genuinely task-free, non-semantic metadata with a frozen target-set and a known exact verifier. A fix applied without this classification is a symptom patch, not SDD.
